chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa al-Kilabi, from Abu al-Hasan (the first) (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman who manumitted her slave girl on condition of manumission (tadbir), and the slave girl gave birth to a valuable female child. The woman did not know whether the born child was also manumitted on condition (mudabbarah) or not. He said to me, 'When was the pregnancy with the manumitted one? Before she manumitted her, or after she manumitted her?' I said, 'I do not know, but answer me for both cases.' He said, 'If the woman manumitted her while she was pregnant and did not specify what was in her womb, then the slave girl is manumitted on condition, and the child is a slave. But if the pregnancy occurred only after the manumission, then the child is manumitted on condition along with the manumission of its mother.'

key_terms.تَدْبِير: Manumission on condition; a slave is freed upon the death of the owner.
key_terms.رِقٌّ: Slavery; the state of being a slave.
key_terms.مُدَبَّرَة: A female slave who has been manumitted on condition.

ai.seo_question: What is the status of a child born to a slave girl after her owner declares her manumission on condition (tadbir)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of 'tadbir' (manumission upon death) is clarified by distinguishing the timing of conception relative to the master's declaration. If the mother was pregnant at the time of manumission without specifying the unborn child, the child remains a slave to preserve the master's estate; however, if conception occurred after the declaration, the child inherits the mother's status and is also manumitted. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the mother's status as the primary determinant for the child's freedom in cases of ambiguous timing.
